raw_ai_output:
```hcl
resource "aws_security_group" "data" {
  name        = "terraveritas-net-c-sg"
  description = "bastion and remote-management host"

  ingress {
    description = "SSH for admin access"
    from_port   = 22
    to_port     = 22
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/16"]
  }

  ingress {
    description = "RDP for Windows admin access"
    from_port   = 3389
    to_port     = 3389
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/16"]
  }
}
```

The finding is triggered by `cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]` on the port 22 (and equally risky port 3389) ingress rule, which opens SSH/RDP admin access to the entire internet. The fix restricts the source to a known, trusted CIDR range (e.g., your corporate VPN or office IP range — replace `10.0.0.0/16` with your actual trusted range) instead of allowing all IPs. For a real deployment, prefer scoping this even tighter to specific `/32` admin IPs, or better yet, remove public ingress entirely and require access via AWS Systems Manager Session Manager or a VPN/bastion in a private subnet.
